Chapter 7: The Love of God—A Surprising Kindness.
You know, love is a word we hear all the time. We use it to describe everything from our favorite foods to the people dearest to us. But when it comes to God, love isn’t just another feeling—it’s something deeper, stronger, and honestly, a bit hard to wrap your head around.
God’s love isn’t sentimental or here one minute and gone the next. No, it’s steady. Fierce. And maybe the most surprising part—completely unearned. This is a love that seeks out those who feel lost, that heals what’s broken, and never, ever gives up.
Picture this for a second. Imagine someone who’s really made a mess of things. Maybe they’ve hurt others, failed themselves, and just run out of excuses. There’s that quiet moment when the noise fades, and all that’s left is a sense of being unworthy, like there’s nothing left to offer.
It’s in those moments—right where you’d least expect it—that God’s love shows up. Not with shame or condemnation, but with this surprising, gentle kindness.
Most people don’t realize just how radical God’s love actually is. It isn’t about how well you perform, or whether you’re worthy. It doesn’t disappear when you mess up. God’s love is anchored in who He is—it’s His very character. That means, no matter how far you’ve wandered, nothing can separate you from it.
I once had a friend who spent years running from God. The reasons were messy—shame, fear, disappointment. But deep down, what scared them most was the thought that maybe God’s love had limits. Maybe it would run out.
But over time, they discovered something beautiful. God’s love is bigger than any failure, deeper than any wound. Realizing that didn’t erase their past, but it changed how they saw their future.
Here’s the thing: God’s love isn’t just a comfort—it’s an invitation. It calls us to live differently. Not because we’re afraid, but because we’re grateful. When you really know you’re loved, you find the courage to forgive, to take risks, to hope again. God’s love isn’t a free pass to do whatever you want—it’s the power to become who you’re meant to be.
Now, maybe you’ve struggled to believe that God’s love is really for you. Maybe you’re carrying old wounds, old lies, or old fears. But the story of God’s love is all about relentless pursuit. It’s about a God who leaves the ninety-nine to find the one who’s wandered off, who welcomes prodigals home with open arms, who never gives up—no matter what.
